name: MonarchAiPermissionScope
title: AiPermissionScope
wrapsNative: VStack of rows with MonarchFavicon; Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) per row when editable; ViewThatFits to stack a row when narrow
summary: What an AI agent may see and change, app by app: each row names the app and the resources it covers and shows No access, Can read or Can read and edit, or a None / Read / Write control when editable.
whenToUse: In agent settings or before an agent runs, to show or change what it may read or edit in each connected app.
whenNotToUse: For one yes-or-no permission use a Toggle (see switch). For system permissions (camera, location) use the system prompt. For per-action approval use the tool-call approval in the conversation.
api: MonarchAiPermissionScope.init(_ scopes: [MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem], labels: MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels = MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels(), onManage: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchAiPermissionScope.init(scopes: Binding<[MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem]>, labels: MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels = MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels(), onManage: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem.init(_ app: String, resources: String? = nil, access: MonarchAiAccessLevel, iconURL: URL? = nil)
enum MonarchAiAccessLevel: Int, Comparable { case none, read, write }

MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels.init(label: String? = nil, access: (@Sendable (MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> String)? = nil, option: (@Sendable (MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> String)? = nil, control: (@Sendable (_ app: String) -> String)? = nil, manage: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil)

options.name: scopes
options.description: One row per app, each with a unique app name, optional resources, the access level and an optional icon URL. An array gives a read-only list; a binding gives a segmented control per row that writes the access.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the list name, the level descriptions, the short option names, the control name, the manage title and the empty text.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Adds a "Manage permissions" button in the Monarch link style.

states.name: read only
states.description: Each row shows the level with a symbol: lock for No access (muted text), eye for Can read, pencil for Can read and edit.

states.name: editable
states.description: Each row has a None / Read / Write segmented control.

states.name: narrow
states.description: When the row does not fit on one line, the access or the control moves under the app name.

states.name: empty
states.description: "The AI has no access to any app." in muted text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With the standard disabled(_:) modifier the controls are dimmed by the system.

appearance: Rows separated by subtle dividers; app names in the default text role and resources in muted text; a favicon or letter tile per app; the system segmented control when editable. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web's manageHref link becomes an onManage closure, since a native app opens its own settings screen. The web's onChange(scopes, changed) becomes a binding. iOS adds an optional app icon through MonarchFavicon. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The list is a container named "What the AI can access".
A read-only row is one element read as the app and its resources, with the access ("Can read") as its value.
Each level has its own symbol as well as its text, so it never depends on colour.
An editable row's control is the system segmented Picker named "Access to <app>".
The favicon is decorative and hidden.
Rows wrap and stack at large text sizes.
edgeCases: App names must be unique: they are the rows' identity.
An empty resources string is not shown or read.
Long app names and resources wrap; the control moves under them.

examples.title: Read-only
examples.template:
MonarchAiPermissionScope([
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem({{scopes.0.app}}, resources: {{scopes.0.resources}}, access: {{scopes.0.access|case}}),
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem({{scopes.1.app}}, resources: {{scopes.1.resources}}, access: {{scopes.1.access|case}}),
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem({{scopes.2.app}}, access: {{scopes.2.access|case}}),
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem({{scopes.3.app}}, access: {{scopes.3.access|case}}),
])
examples.code:
MonarchAiPermissionScope([
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem("Calendar", resources: "Your events only", access: .read),
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem("Documents", resources: "Shared projects", access: .write),
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem("Contacts", access: .read),
    MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem("Billing", access: .none),
])
